stem: A web shop team tests each release candidate by hand and is now automating its existing regression checks. It has set four goals for testing the next release. Which goal does that automation directly deliver?

options.text: The same checks run identically on every build, with results back sooner than the manual run.
The redesigned checkout page is judged for how easy first-time shoppers find it to use.
The new loyalty scheme is explored for behaviour that its written requirements do not describe.
The features that carry the most business risk are identified before testing effort is allocated.

rationale: Key a: automating an existing set of checks makes them run identically on every build and return their results far sooner than a manual run, which is the direct objective of test automation: consistent, repeatable execution with fast feedback. b is wrong because how easy a page is to use is a human judgement with no expected result that a script can compare against, so it remains a manual testing activity. c is wrong because an automated check can only compare behaviour against the expected result it was given; exploring a feature for behaviour that nobody has specified is exploratory testing performed by a person, and although automation may free time for it, it does not perform it. d is wrong because identifying which features carry the most business risk is an analysis made by people before checks are chosen; automation executes the checks that this judgement selects, it does not make the judgement.
sourceAnchor: ISTQB CTAL-TAE v2 (Udemy) - Chapter 1 Introduction and objectives for test automation: purpose of automation, advantages and limitations, automation versus manual testing
